notes: Rust entrypoint for FastSurfer-style conformation; Python method loads, conditionally conforms, saves the conformed file, and returns the conformed image plus ndarray.
Both load image data together with header and affine context; Rust also converts mgz/mgh to a temporary NIfTI when needed.
Rust explicit options correspond to the kwargs assembled by RunModelOnData before calling is_conform and conform.
Both check whether the volume already satisfies FastSurfer conformation criteria for voxel size, image size, dtype uint8, and orientation.
Both derive the target voxel size and target image shape from vox_size, img_size, and threshold_1mm semantics.
Rust subset that implements vox_size=min or explicit value or any and the threshold-to-1mm rule.
Both derive or validate orientation codes from the affine basis.
Both perform the actual conformation pipeline: compute target geometry, resample into target space, rescale intensities, round to uint8, and return the conformed volume.
Rust constructs the target affine directly; Python populates an MGHHeader and then uses header.get_affine to obtain the same target-space affine.
Both write the target shape, zooms, datatype, and affine metadata for the conformed output image.
Rust encodes target axis basis vectors directly for the requested orientation; Python builds orientation transforms via nibabel orientation arrays.
Both normalize the source affine basis when preserving native orientation semantics.
Rust scales orientation basis columns by target zooms before affine assembly, matching the role of Mdc and delta in the Python header construction.
Equivalent to the numpy.linalg.inv usage inside Python map_image when forming vox2vox and inv_vox2vox.
Both resample the source volume into the target grid using affine mapping and linear interpolation; Python can also take a no-interpolation reorder or crop fast path.
Common affine point transform used while building or sampling target-space coordinates.
Rust interpolation kernel used by resample_linear_volume.
Rust out-of-bounds handling returns zero, matching the zero-padding behavior used by crop_transform or affine_transform in Python.
Both compute robust rescaling parameters from the original intensity histogram before mapped data is converted to the output range.
Rust combines Python's scalecrop step with the final rint plus clip-to-uint8 behavior performed later in conform.
Rust-only compatibility shim because the Rust nifti reader cannot read mgz directly; Python load_image delegates to nibabel which already supports mgz or mgh input.
Native Rust loader without FastSurfer conformation; included because controller tests previously compared against this lower-level loading boundary.
Both resolve qform or sform consistency and reject invalid affine or voxel-size combinations; Rust returns the chosen affine while Python updates the nibabel image in place.
Rust helper that reconstructs the sform affine directly from header fields; Python relies on nibabel's header accessors.
Rust helper that reconstructs the qform affine directly from quaternion fields; Python uses nibabel get_qform.
Rust-only fallback used when neither sform nor qform is set.
